whyItMatters: Varices are dilated veins that form when portal hypertension diverts blood through the oesophageal veins. Cirrhosis is the most common cause. A variceal bleed can be massive and life-threatening.
treatment: Endoscopic band ligation and nonselective beta blockers prevent bleeding. An acute bleed needs resuscitation with terlipressin, antibiotics, and urgent endoscopy.

findings: Frontal (AP/PA) upright-appearing chest and upper abdomen radiograph during a contrast (barium) esophagram.
Barium-filled esophagus runs along the left of the spine, with a smooth, tapered distal end.
The distal esophagus narrows into a beak-like tapering at the gastroesophageal junction, with a thin stream of contrast entering the stomach.

The mid-to-distal esophagus has an irregular, serpiginous, corrugated mucosal pattern with filling defects, in keeping with retained food or debris and contrast mixing, plus tertiary-like contour irregularity.
The proximal and upper esophagus is mildly dilated and filled with a dense column of barium.
A gastric fundus with a barium pool and an air-fluid level or gas bubble lies below the left hemidiaphragm.
The lungs are clear without a large effusion or focal consolidation.
The cardiac silhouette is not enlarged, and the thoracic spine shows mild degenerative change or scoliosis-like curvature.
differential: Achalasia (primary) with distal bird-beak narrowing and a retained food/debris-filled esophagus
Pseudoachalasia from a distal esophageal or gastroesophageal junction tumor causing malignant stricture
Distal esophageal stricture from peptic or other benign disease, or a motility disorder such as Chagas disease
anatomyConcerns: No impossible anatomy is evident. The esophageal course, beak tapering and gastric position are plausible.
The esophagus appears to lie slightly left of midline with mild spinal curvature, which is likely positional or a normal variant.
Image rotation, an edge crop and a dark border on the right do not affect interpretation.
The serpiginous filling defects are likely retained food or air within the barium column, not an anatomic anomaly.

clueFacts.fact: Constant tiredness is common in the cirrhosis that typically underlies oesophageal varices because liver failure, anaemia, and poor nutrition can all cause fatigue.

clueFacts.clue: a belly that kept getting bigger
clueFacts.fact: A belly that kept getting bigger often reflects ascites from portal hypertension and low albumin in cirrhosis, the same pressure that typically produces oesophageal varices.
